title: $\gamma_d$ is surjective for $d\geq g$
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], of genus $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus]. For $d\in\mathbf Z$ let $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$ be the subfunctor of the Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ [def-pc-picard-functor] on $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ of the classes whose fibrewise degree [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] is identically $d$. Let $d\geq g$, let $H_d$ be a $k$-scheme representing $\operatorname{Hilb}^d_{C/k}$ [def-pc-hilb-functor], let $P_d$ be a $k$-scheme representing $\operatorname{Pic}^d_{C/k}$, and let $\gamma_d:H_d\to P_d$ be the morphism $D\mapsto\mathcal O(D)$ of [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]. Then $\gamma_d$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clause (5) 'the morphisms gamma_d are surjective for d >= g', and its proof, fourth paragraph: 'Let d >= g. Then for any field extension K/k and any invertible O_{X_K}-module L of degree d, chi(X_K, L) = d+1-g > 0. Hence L has a nonzero section and we conclude that L = O_{X_K}(D) for some divisor D of degree d. It follows that gamma_d is surjective'

proof.text: For each p in P take K to be an algebraic closure of its residue field. The canonical geometric point x : Spec K -> P maps the unique point to p. By the existing source theorem exists_toSheafify_app_eq_of_isAlgClosed, x has a representative LK in the degree-d Picard subpresheaf. This suffices for topological surjectivity; a rational point on the original curve and the normalized Picard splitting are unnecessary.

Base change C to K. The existing smoothOfRelativeDimension_and_isProper_and_geometricallyIntegral_pullback_snd gives smoothness of relative dimension one, properness and integrality; GlobalSectionsBijective.of_geometricallyIntegral gives H0(O)=K. Arithmetic genus is preserved by arithmeticGenus_pullback. The private proved helper exists_abelClass_eq_of_genus_le evaluates membership of LK at the identity field point to get degree(LK)=d, uses eulerChar_eq_degree_add and eulerChar_eq_finrankH_zero_sub_finrankH_one to obtain h0(LK)>0 by integer arithmetic from genus<=d, and obtains a nonzero section.

Take the zero scheme D of the nonzero section morphism. On the integral curve the source locally-principal zero-locus theorem makes its ideal invertible (the zero-locus-equals-bottom criterion rules out the zero morphism). Hom.nonempty_iso_dual_toModules_tensorObj and the right unitor identify LK with O(D). The smooth-proper-curve finiteness theorem isFinite_subschemeι_comp makes D finite, without the general proper-dimension-at-most-one CartierDivisorFinite theorem. degree_dual_toModules and degree_congr give its global-section rank d. Flatness and local finite presentation over the field are instances; finrank_eq_fiberDegree and fiberDegree_eq_finrankΓ give constant degree d. Thus D is a Hilbert point, and abelClassIso identifies its Abel class with LK.

Use hD and abelClassIso to show that L equals the Abel class of the universal Hilbert divisor. Hence hγ identifies γ with the morphism induced by abelMapPresheaf. Naturality of eH.homEquiv, eP.homEquiv, abelMapPresheaf and toSheafify proves the corresponding classifying formula hab for every T->H. Send D through eH.homEquiv.symm to obtain h : Spec K->H. The equality of its Abel class with LK and the representative equality from the first step give eP.homEquiv(h >> γ)=eP.homEquiv(x). Injectivity gives h >> γ=x.
Apply the underlying-map equality h >> γ=x to the unique point of Spec K. Its image under x is p by Scheme.fromSpecResidueField_apply. Thus every p has a preimage, proving Surjective γ.left.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 0BA0, proof, fourth paragraph, read in pic.tex (tag verified in tags/tags). The single sentence is written out in seven steps: (1) C has a k-point (separably closed k), so C_K is a smooth projective curve with H^0=K, h^1=g, cohomology vanishing above 1, chi = h^0 - h^1 and chi(O)=1-g; (2) a K-point y of P_d is a class xi in Pic^d(Spec K), represented by an invertible L on C_K (Pic(C_K) -> Pic_{C/k}(Spec K) onto by 0B9N/0B9U) of degree d (degree of a class through the trivial covering); (3) chi(L)=d+1-g>=1 so h^0(L)>=1 (no Riemann-Roch theorem is needed: the degree is defined as chi(L)-chi(O)); (4) on the integral C_K, Z(s) of a nonzero s is an effective Cartier divisor D and L = O(D) (two new nodes, Stacks 02OR(4)/01WZ and 01X0(2)); (5) D is finite over K of length deg O(D) = d, so finite locally free of degree d, a K-point of Hilb^d; (6) its point x of H_d satisfies gamma_d o x = y by clause (3) of [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism]; (7) with K = kappa(p) every point p of P_d is hit. Statement unchanged. No slopmaster2 declaration states the item (grep of the id, of 'Hilb' and of Picard/Jacobian.lean: the surjectivity is only described in the docstring of the sorry isProper_of_representableBy_picardFunctorDegree_genus). Tools of other units used as black boxes: lem-pc-cartier-divisor-finite-over-field and lem-pc-degree-base-change (sk-thm-picard-rr), prop-pc-xk-integral and lem-pc-vanishing-above-dim (sk-thm-picard-twist), lem-pc-rational-hyp/thm-pc-pic-split (sk-prop-picard-pic-split), lem-pc-rational-points-dense (sk-prop-picard-dense-points), lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined (sk-thm-picard-rr); all are units the unit sk-prop-jacobian cites, directly or through them.
